expectations.text: States who qualifies as a beginner in words that could be argued only one way
expectations.evidence: The brief defines a first-timer tightly: 'someone who has never submitted a project to any hackathon, in person or online, student or professional. Attending a hackathon without submitting does not count against you.' That closes the main loopholes (online, student, attended only). Two gaps remain. First, the registration checkbox reads 'This is my first hackathon', but the definition is about having submitted a project, so a person who attended earlier without submitting could read the checkbox two ways. expectations.evidence: The brief gives fairly concrete rules. A team qualifies if every member meets at least one of two conditions: they have 'never completed a hackathon project before Loop Hack', or they have 'less than 1 year of programming experience, counting study, bootcamps, and self-teaching'. Any member who 'has worked as a professional software developer' or 'has won a hackathon prize before' makes the team ineligible. The response also argues for objective cutoffs ('can be checked'). Several terms can still be read more than one way. 'Completed a hackathon project' could mean submitted, finished, or atte
